title: App keeps getting better
body:
This is by far the best habit tracker in App Store. I have, however, two improvement requests:

1- Add setting to always show best streak. Right now the only way to see the best streak is by having at least three check-ins in a row. Not having that visible at all times is demotivating if you broke the chain and you are trying to recover.

2- Drag and drop from main view. The only way to reorder now is by going to the settings. This is not the best scenario since I am reordering the habits by the effectivity all the time to focus on the ones that need improvement.

PLEASE add those improvements and I will update the review to 5 stars.

title: Cleanest space to track and reflect
body: I rarely make $ contributions but jumped at the chance to ‘tip’ the developers. I’ve tried many different tracking and journaling apps but I feel Way of Life is the perfect balance between a. putting things down, and b. being able to review later. Firstly, it’s not fidgety to mark yes or to write a journal entry which means I can be consistent. Secondly, the multi month view gives me such a quick look at my progress. Way of Life also has the BEST excel export I’ve tried if I want to nerd out. title: Excellent!
body:
I've tried loads of habit-changing/to-do apps and this is so far the best one. 
I love that you can go back a few days and add what you did, even if you forgot to do it on the actual day - which means you don't lose your progress and you get a better analysis. 
Adding notes to things is also another great feature, because you can explain why you failed to achieve it that day. 
Many of these apps leave you feeling like you have failed because you missed a day or two, which not only results in no longer wanting to use it, but also diminishes the likelihood that you will keep up the good habits you're trying to achieve. 

The design is fairly basic but I don't think that is a bad thing, it is easy to read and learn to use which again, is another plus compared to other, unnecessarily complex, apps.

I would love to see a few more things in there like perhaps the ability to add goals and goal dates and rewards and so on to condition the habits and keep track of successes.

Great app!

title: Good, but could be great
body:
Great idea - and sweet app! I can see myself using this every day and suggesting it to a LOT of people.
However, I'd like to give feedback that could move the product forward.

1
Scrolling tap.
In journal, the current green/red/skip entry mechanic feels clunky. How about tap once on a day for green, tap twice for red, tap three times for skip? Or hold finger on the day and the three colours pop up in a menu (same UX as if you hold your finger on an iOS keyboard character?)

2
Set default skip days when creating new habit.
ie, when creating a new habit the user is presented with a week view template on which they can choose their default, recurring 'skip' days. If I'm doing yoga twice a week it's annoying to have to continually, manually enter 'skip' for the other five days, it'd be nice if I set those skips days on a template when I first created the habit so I didn't have to keep re-entering them.

3
Upcoming habits.
It'd be fun to create future habits that sit inactive, perhaps below in the journal. I can set a date they go live, or activate them when I'm ready. This also serves to keep the user engaged with the app.

Thanks and good luck!

title: Great app, but sad about losing the premium subscription discount
body:
Hi team, the app is awesome, no improvement feedback on my side. 
However, I think commercially-wise it’s not te best that you only offer a reduced price in the first days after installation. In my opinion, it should be given after several days of usage when the person already explores full benefits and is ready to make this commitment. I was pretty frustrated when I didn’t have a chance to get the subscription at the reduced rate exactly in the moment when I decided app was valuable enough for me to do the purchase. Exactly in that moment the price has increased for me, and I ended up not subscribing, feeling like I “lost my chance” already. Maybe you can do an A/B test with newly acquired users, offering a temporary discount in the first vs second week of usage to check which results in a higher engagement and subscription rate. And you can also give the discount to me again :) 
Thanks and all the best

title: Back up your data
body: I had been using Way of Life daily for over four years to track all of my habits, including medications. I loved using the app and it worked great, until one day I downloaded an update and all of my data disappeared. I incorrectly believed that the data was linked to my account, when it actually is not linked to anything at all and needed to be manually backed up in order to be saved. I was super disappointed by this, as I lost many streaks of over 1000 days, as well as important medical information, because this information was not shared anywhere. I think it is a great app to use for habits if you’re willing to manually backed-up your data on a regular basis, but I will be switching to an app that actually stores the data in your account so you do not have to take this extra step.

title: LOCKED OUT OF APP
body:
I am locked out of my app 😡 and have zero way to get back in.

I saw there was a password protection feature so I wanted to try it.

It was asking me to put a pin password in on a numeric keypad. At first I put in a pin and I did put it in a second time to confirm it because I saw there was a faceID button and I preferred that over a pin. 

The app LET ME register FaceID WITHOUT registering a pin password, and under the password section I saw FaceID listed there with a toggle button to turn it on and off. 

Then I decided I didn’t like it and wanted to turn FACEID off so turned off the toggle button off for FaceID. I ASSUMED that this meant the password was off since I was allowed to register FACEID WITHOUT registering a pin.

Now every time I open the app all I see is a keypad to put in my pin (which never existed in the first place). The pin I put in once is not working because I didn’t confirm it.

There is also a FaceID button but this does not work since the toggle is off. 

I was allowed to register FaceID without registering a pin and now I am locked out of the app.

DO NOT USE THEIR PASSWORD PROTECTION just use IOS 18’s FaceID.

Now I have no idea how to get my information back and might lose over a years worth of data.

The backups on my iCloud are from 2023.

Feb 20, 2024… almost 9 years since my last review and 13 since the first. In the past 9 years I’ve tried other habit tracking apps because I’m a bit of an app junky, but I can confidently say it’s still the best in class. Definitely the app I’ve used the longest on iOS.
-------------------------
March 5, 2015 Still use the app daily and it's still the best tracking app of its kind. 
 ------------------------- 
 July 16, 2014 It's been about 4 years since my first review and I still stand by all of them. I use this app daily because it's reliable, fast and provides meaningful data at a quick glance. I now track 8 items and I'm in and out of the app in seconds (10-15 usually unless I'm looking at stats). The upgrade was icing on the cake. :) 
 ------------------------- 
 Jan 11, 2012 I wanted to update my review as I've used the app daily for over a year now. I've tried to replace it with others (seeking the next best thing) but nothing compares to the ease of use. It's still as simple and as effective as ever. Even more so since their update a while back. Worth every penny. 
 -------------------------

title: Best Habit Tracker I’ve tried.
body:
I've been using Way of Life for a while now, and it's honestly been a game-changer in how I approach my daily habits. The app's design is clean and intuitive, making it incredibly easy to track my progress with just a few taps. Whether it's building new healthy habits or breaking old ones, Way of Life has empowered me to be more accountable and consistent. The unique color-coded system and the ability to see long-term trends are particularly motivating, pushing me to stay on track.

However, there's one feature I find myself wishing for - the ability to collaborate and share progress with friends or family. Many habit-tracking apps offer this social aspect, which can significantly boost motivation and accountability through shared goals and friendly competition. While Way of Life excels in personal habit tracking, adding a feature for collaboration and sharing could elevate the experience to new heights, fostering a sense of community and support among users.

In summary, Way of Life is an outstanding habit tracker that has made a noticeable difference in my life. It's straightforward, effective, and almost perfect. If you're looking to make meaningful changes in your habits, this app is definitely worth trying out. Here's hoping future updates might include the option to collaborate with others, making it not just a personal journey, but a shared one too.

After successfully using the app for several months, and believing I had developed good habits , I stopped for 2 months ... I gained weight, was tired, work performed dropped, and home life degraded .. Things got better once I started to use the app again .. I now consider this app essential to keep my life in top gear.
The user interface is a pleasure to use because it is quick to enter my results each day. and the ability to customize habits to my needs is very important. 

I recommend you start slow, just a few simple habits.. Once you experience success, then add more.

title: The (Good) Habit-Forming App You Want!
body:
I've been looking for an app like this for a long time and I'm thrilled to finally come across Way of Life.

The closest I was able to find were the habit-forming apps by Jaidev Soin on the App Store. They looked great and did their job, but eventually they just became apps in the background that became 'too much of a hassle' to use (i.e. they didn't motivate me enough to stop being lazy).

Way of Life is incredibly easy to use, yet flexible enough to be customised to your personal needs and goals. Plus, something about being able to keep up those greens make me want to keep the trend going. Even if I didn't fulfill a goal / habit, there's a certain satisfaction to be gained from tapping on the checks, crosses and skips (perhaps it's all those colours).

If you're the type of person who wants to be productive, but sometimes needs motivation to stop being so lazy, then this could be the app you want. Double thumbs up!

Bug: When adding a note to the bottom entries (specifically when you have a lot of entries), the keyboard hides the note section so you can't see what you're typing. No other bugs / issues otherwise. Amazing app, thank you!

title: Great app but could use a few more features to be amazing

Way of life is great at getting you to do exactly what it claims to do: track your habits in a yes/no/not applicable rating scale. It doesn't seem to be v actively developed (according to the nudge that got me to rate the app I've been using the same version for over 9 months). 

Update: turns out nudge is wrong. Current version is about 2 months old. The chain feature is new. Yay!

It is missing a couple of features that would make me rate it 5 stars such as: customizable rating scales, and ability to pull in data to correlate with habit data from other sources. That said, I'm glad it doesn't have some awful social component built in. 

TLDR: it's an awesome app that will probably suit most but maybe not all of your needs with regard to habit tracking.

title: Great App
body: This app is the main app on my iphone.  I consider myself a heavy user as it allows me to plan and execute in the areas that matter to me.  Forming new habits? No problem! Setting goals for the day based on where I need to be overall.  Yes can do that too.  The best feature in my opinion is the viewing options for different ways to see notes.  I am an extensive note taker and to be able to see the notes in relation to each day as well as in relation to each tag, makes planning easy.  I could use the notes alone to look back and notice trends in my overall consistencies.  This has helped me to see that a part of my problem is that I am setting unrealistic objectives for the day in some cases and therefore I needed to scale back to ensure  that there was enough hours in the day to meet the goals I set.  I have requested some other features from the developer that would make this a five star program but is it still worth a review to me.

title: Customizable and user-friendly
body:

You can even set up a daily reminder to use the app! Tracking options are yes/no/neutral, so you can even allow yourself a rest day without it counting as a no. title: Helps make habits stick
body:
I've used a half dozen different apps over the years to try and track habits. This is the first one that I've been really satisfied with. The UI is very good and gets out if your way after using it once or twice. It took me all of five minutes to set up the habits I want to track ( it has a selection of popular predefined habits  already available but you can also specify your own). It takes me on average a minute a day to update and review my progress.  It offers several views of the progress you've made on each habit through pie charts, bar graphs and trending lines. 
 Unlike other similar apps I've tried this one allows you to define habits your trying to avoid as well as those you are trying to form. It also allows you to go back to previous days and input data you may have missed after the fact. 
 This one sits on the home page of my iPhone.

title: Best of the Bunch
body:
I've tried almost all the food, exercise, and general tracking apps, and I can tell you this app is the best of the bunch.  It has programming finesse, an attractive and easy-to-use interface, and it's fully customisable. 

I'm using it to track lots of things: whether I lost weight, flossed, took vitamins, brought lunch to work, left work on time, exercised (good), ate sugar, ate refined grains, drank caffeine, drank alcohol (bad if more than one serving).  In the future, I might use it to track music practice, meditation, sleep, moods, stress, etc.  Over time, it's possible to see patterns and linkages between the items tracked. 

There is only one thing I would add to the app if I could, and that is a way to track when I do a thing more than once in a day. For example, I want to indicate (easily, with a click) each time I eat a serving of sugar, so that at the end of the day I know how many I've had. Right now, I can use notes to record servings, quantities, timings, reps, sets, distances, or whatever, which offers total flexibility. But it's not easy to see at a glance for each separate item tracked which days are better than others, and whether there's improvement over time. 

Programming the above would require a toggle to indicate which items are quantifiable, and then a separate, item-specific graph page to track and display quantities per day/week/month/year. 

Even without that functionality, though, it's a well-designed and useful tracking app. Highly recommended.

title: Poor service from developer
body:
I upgraded to the premium version of the app but I noticed that some of the stats were not working correctly. I took screen prints and sent questions to the developer but they didn't bother responding. In fact, I followed up three times and they never even acknowledged my query which I think is very poor. 

The app itself is ok but frankly nothing you can't on excel. The stats were very important to me and since these don't work properly, I got my money back and will use another app to track my habits. Shame on the "developers" who took the money and ran.

My advice, use the free version of this app (and track 3 habits - just bundle your habits together) and don't part with your money.

title: 使用八个月后点评way of life
body:
2020.01.24
继续支持，继续使用，两年了
————————————————————2019.08更新评论：
 • 收费，收费怎么了？免费给你用？
不买又想便宜用，你怕是贪便宜成习惯了！
 • 最近一次更新，色彩改变太丑了！估计卖主题才是目的！
————————————————————
• 相比其它习惯追踪软件，重点更突出于记录，非常棒的思路
 • 可视化效果非常优秀，泾渭分明
 • 我不止用于习惯追踪，我已经当成了我的生活记录软件，
 • 我的特点是，越用就越寻求更偷懒的办法，我现在已经习惯只打勾，不会打❌了，其实效果差不多。
 • 对于评论里有人说的奖励机制，我只想说这是十分白痴的建议，软件里的奖励机制不足以满足你脑子里的化学物质，你需要的是自己给自己奖励，而不是软件给你奖励，stupied guys 。
 • 寻找新意——这是我努力对抗厌倦的方法。

开发者太良心了！直接增加八个主题并且移除免费版界面提醒开通pro的banner ！cool！

title: 一点功能增进建议
body: 作为一个购买了软件的用户，感觉这个软件的主要价值是对个人习惯的总结分析（认清楚自己有多糟糕），但是除了笔记有总结问题的功能外，没有一个更有效的激励机制，比如连续7天全都标绿，可以达成一个奖励。其他软件那种勋章什么的好无聊，建议是可以自定义内容，并把达成目标后的奖励作为提醒内容的一项。另外把“他人监督”作为社交的方式，一键分享成果到朋友圈微博（目前只有企鹅有点局限），而且分享形式只有一个图，缺乏一些模版式结论或者自定义下阶段目标，全红可以强制如“我是懒蛋”的耻辱play一类的，增加社交趣味。当然不乏很多人喜欢这种性冷淡设计，但“他人监督”这一点上再下一些功夫总没错。

title: 我有建议要提
body:
1.目前定性习惯的变量是二元变量:好与不好。缺少频次的选择。比如一件事我一天必须做两次，少了或多了都不好，我需要自定义好与不好的规则。
1.2自定义规则里除了次数还可以增设奇偶数，比如奇数次好，偶数次坏。之所以要记录次数，是因为在形成习惯和总结行为时，用户会需要用到更细的过程，而不是结果，做了和没做。而是做了后做了多少多做多少少做多少总共多少？，没做多少，将就了多少？比如我一天要做10组动作，可我只做了9组累了，或者有电话来了，停了。这样怎么记录，目前只能选备注一下？这不够好。

现在的软件把这部分记录次数的行为交给用户的记性，单纯只留下二元选项好与不好。这这不利于用户打开软件的次数，原因:如果记录下行为频次，就可以每周每月每年都有相关数据的报表，查看后能得到很多深度反馈的信息。

优点大家已经说了，我来提一下，还有一个重要功能可以提升：有些任务不单单是每日完成了那样简单，还有完成的额度需要记录、汇总统计，趋势表格可以分开两项查看，1.每日坚持情况
2.每日的任务完成量，如果能加上这个功能，真是做梦都要笑醒了！到时我要大大安利给身边很多和我一样需求的人！

title: 总体不错，细节须改进
body:
试用了感觉不错就买了，每天都用，也慢慢养成了一些好习惯。
细节需要改进：
1、已设置的项目名称不能修改
2、项目调整的过程有点让人疑惑，是试出来的，希望今后能考虑易用性多一些
3、能否增加一点有用的小功能，如我需要锻炼10分钟，能否内置一个时间提醒，这样就完美了
4、备份可以，但不能导入，加入导入历史数据功能就好了。但是最完美的是支持Evernote同步，有时候我用ipad，有时候用iPhone，数据同步的话会很方便。

title: Der beste Habittracker
body:
Als ich vor etwa 5 Jahren nach einem sinnvollen Habit Tracker gesucht habe, bin ich auf die unterschiedlichsten Apps gestoßen - bessere und schlechtere. Ich habe versucht, meine Gewohnheiten mit ihnen zu messen, aber in jeder von ihnen hat mich am Ende etwas irritiert und ich bin zu Way of Life zurückgekehrt, das damals wie heute meine Nummer eins ist - dank seiner Einfachheit, Eleganz und Funktionalität.

Es gibt hier keine Feuerwerke, keine Gamification oder andere Dinge, die vielleicht nett fürs Auge sind, aber in Wirklichkeit oft nur ablenken und vom Wesentlichen wegführen. 

Mehrmals habe ich mich gefragt, ob mir in dieser App nicht die Möglichkeit fehlt, eine teilweise Erledigung zu markieren.
Letztlich komme ich jedoch zum Schluss, dass der Entwickler - wieder im Geist der Einfachheit und des Gewohnheitenaufbaus - die richtige Entscheidung getroffen hat, nämlich drei Optionen anzubieten: erledigt, nicht erledigt, übersprungen.
Eine teilweise Markierung ergibt, wenn man genauer darüber nachdenkt, eigentlich wenig Sinn - entweder man hat etwas gemacht oder nicht. Wenn man krank war oder aus einem anderen Grund etwas nicht tun konnte, wählt man übersprungen. Und genau in dieser Einfachheit liegt der Wert dieser App.

title: Excellence in Simplicity
body: Simple, intuitive app without much overhead that does exactly what it is intended to: Track how you do on your self-chosen way-of-life practices, every day. The red and green design encourages honesty and determination: you either accomplished your goal or you didn‘t. Focus on what’s important, don’t cheat yourself. The grouping of goals by label and the button for not-yet-updated goals are very handy and make logging take maybe half a minute for all 17 entries that I have. Starting and staying on your streaks is very rewarding and gives nice visual feedback via a chain of marked green-day entries. The length of your streak is indicated in a nice box that also shows you when you reach your self-set target streak-length. The statistics tab is well organized and contains all relevant information. It doesn‘t have many options, though, which I think is a plus because I imagine that otherwise I would spend quite some time browsing the statistics to see how well I have done. Also the minimum period that you can chose for display is six weeks, which subtly communicates to the user that this is an app for serious long-term progress (allthough I found it particularly motivating for new users as myself that you can have your first streak already on the third day and hence some early in-app sense of success). A feature worth mentioning are the well-made reminders that you can link to bring you directly to the not-yet-updated goals of a given label. I have set labels and reminders for ‚morning‘, ‚day‘ and ‚evening‘ and can then go through those list with only 1 click per item. More efficiency is impossible! The only feature I am missing - or haven‘t found yet - is to set journal entries (=goals) to inactive (or archieve them) so that you can save their statistics but don‘t have them clutter your todo list. Not every daily habit is made for eternity, like for example studying daily for some exam or doing recovery exercises till they are no longer needed. I recommend this app, it is a great tool. Use it to your benefit!

title: Good but missing some features
body: I like this app. It is quick and easy to use, and I keep track of things I would like to do but never get around to doing. There are, however,  features missing that I would expect to see in a paid app. For example, I cannot sync between devices automatically-I have to do it manually with back up and restore. Also, I am not able to count with this app. I would like to count the number of minutes of exercise I do per week but I can only choose between yes or no or skip. In general, it is a good app if you are looking to improve your daily habits, but not so intuitive if you are looking to improve your weekly habits.

title: Simple, efficace et ouvert
body:
Pour que l'exercice de suivi de ses habitides perdure, il doit être smple a réaliser. C'est le cas avec cette app, ce n'est pas fastidieux de noter ses habitudes, et de se motiver pour garder les bonnes et s'affranchir des mauvaises.

Très important, il est très facil d'exporter les résultats.

Une seule limite, on ne peut tracker que toute le journée. Par exemple, vous pourrez marquer une journée comme quoi vous avez fumé ou pas, mais pas compter le nombre se cigarette consommées. C'est le revers de la médaille pour un outil aussi simple.

title: No customer support at all
body:
I used to be a happy user of Way of Life and even paid for the premium version. However, after switching to a new phone, I discovered that I can no longer access the premium features I had paid for.

I tried reaching out to Way of Life through multiple channels — email, social media — but received no response at all. It’s extremely frustrating that a product marketed as a one-time purchase does not actually carry over when you change devices. Even with my original email and account, there’s no clear way to restore access to what I paid for.

What’s even more disappointing is the complete lack of customer support. It feels like there is no one behind the product. If you ever run into issues, you’re on your own.

I would caution others before buying the premium version. Be aware that your purchase may only last as long as your current device. Sadly, the customer support is practically non-existent, which makes the whole experience very frustrating.

title: Useful and clear app
body:
I like this as an easy way of recording fitness and health data without turning me into a function of my phone. I use it as a journal but you can do a lot more if you chose.
It has enough it can do and I’d say it’s worth investing in the premium version for even more features.
There are slightly more complicated apps for those who want to spend most of the day recording everything they do like checking how much their VO2 Max has changed since that cheese sandwich and guilty sit down for fifteen seconds while Joe Wicks is blinking.
This app is ideal for those like me hellbent on remaining human.
I think most people are going to like having this app on their gadget in case another gadget in the house declares war on them. It’s handy for those moments we’ve all experienced, waking up at 4am to find Jack Dorsey meditating you to death and Jeff Bezos navigating a drone at the exercise bike you spent £10,000 on because you didn’t have something to hide in the hallway cupboard at the end of January.
Good application.

title: does one thing and does it well
body:
great app, if you start using this, your productivity and well being really will improve. Great that you only pay once to switch to premium, and not a monthly or yearly subscription. 

Some other people have complained you cant set a frequency for a habit (eg no junk food for 5 out of 7 days). Instead you just put the number in the title (eg exercise 4 days this week), then you just put 'skip' for the days when you don't exercise. It's up to you to put an (X) for a day when you have broken the chain: eg exercise for 4 days might be : Y-Y--YX .. because you got to the end of the week and hadn't exercised 4 times. At first I was also looking for the option for x per week or x per month on a task, but this way is actually much more flexible and easier. Just thought I'd mention that as it's not in any tutorial/instructions!

title: One day at a time
body:
Today marks day 7 of using the app, I immediately signed up for Premium- amazing value for money. I recently saw the doctor regarding my mental health. I am due to start some CBT this coming week. I needed something to help me stay motivated for the little things that help me as a human being. This app for me is like a speedy version of a bullet journal without the stress of carrying a book and pens with it, everywhere I go. I like the notes button where for each goal it displays all notes written in chronological (descending ) order. It's very well thought out. They've kept UI simple and easy on the eye too. Great!! After it updated all my data was still there-phew !! I like simple, good looking and practical - this app ticks all of these requirements. It's helping me track where I'm at. I really like the skip option - as I don't train everyday and ticking skip rather than no is great for motivation! When I do actually accidentally miss a goal I click no but choosing to skip a day as part of maintaining recovery period and having a sensible app that knows about skip is terrific. Definitely recommend!!

title: HIGHLY Recommended!
body: What a beautiful app. The simplicity of it is what makes it beautiful. The colour code using green and red to mark whether you did or did not complete your goal. And grey to represent a skipped day. For example. You were sick that day and you couldn't make it to the gym. You don't have to feel bad by giving yourself a red box. Because it's not your fault you can't go. Mark it as skipped. And if you want. You can even write a note in that box saying I was sick today. And I love that you can create any, and endless amount of goals/habits. And it gives you ideas on what to make as a good or bad goals/habits. Which I think are all great ideas. And of course I can't leave without mentioning the amazing chart breakdown. To see your progress over time like that is priceless. This app really is the app to keep you on track. Whether it is to keep you motivated to keep your gym sessions consistent or kick that bad habit of smoking. This app is for everyone. It will be one of the few apps that will earn its way to your main screen of your phone.

This app is always there to remind me about what I need to do to move towards having good days. I will write to the programmer and request for a month/year view. Something which allows me to see a snapshot of all the good and bad days for 2012. If you want to form habits, there ain't a better app right now than this one.

title: I love this app!
body:

But two suggestions. A, please improve the look and colour schemes. You can definitely give it a more polished feel. B, I need habit categories. Work habits, food habits, behaviour habits, etc. You should let me keep different sets of habits and view them in groups. 

Thanks!

title: Love this app
body:
Pros: Extremely easy to use and in less than 2 minutes you can tick as many items as you wish with your choice. red/green bars also make it easy to visually analyze the trend of that particular activity. Amidst other applications which do similar activity, I find this most user-friendly and slick. Works well with the iPad in 1x and 2x mode but would really appreciate a separate app with similar UI.

Cons: I think its a bit expensive at $3.99. Maybe I'll wait for a holiday sale of some kind to purchase this app.

それだけでも満足だが、さらにマメな人は、日付ごとに日記のようにメモを取ることもできるのでこれも活用するともっとやる気が続くかもしれない。

body:

グラフ数値も、回数と%の2通りの表示方法があり、振り返る時非常に便利。
メモした日は、評価欄の右上が折られた風になるのもわかりやすくて素敵なデザインだな、と思います。
アラームでお知らせしてくれるのですが、それを無視する習慣がついてしまい、それさえなければ確実に習慣化できると思います。

「やらなかったのか？」それとも「記入し忘れたのか？」が区別できますので、習慣の達成度を正しく振り返ることができます。

title: 良いですね。
body:
使ってみた印象です。
習慣づけたい項目の書き方は
スナックを我慢した、ではなく、
スナックを食べた、と「しなかったこと」ではなく「したこと」を書くことですね。
書自分がやめたいけどやめられないことを、全て書き出すことで、自分の悪い習慣を整理、可視化できます。
書き出すだけでも、抑止とモチベーションアップにも多少はつながるようです。
項目を書き出したらあとは毎日ボタンを押すだけなので楽です。
それも面倒ならダメですけどね。

title: 습관 관리하기 좋은 어플 :)
body:

1) '함/안함' 체크 외에 '건너뛰기'도 할 수 있어서 마음먹고 안한 날(?)에 죄책감없이 기록할 수 있음
2) 간단히 노트를 쓸 수 있어 실천하면서 들었던 생각이나 느낌을 생생히 적을 수 있음
3) 백업기능이 있어 날아갈 걱정 없음
4) 실천추이가 그래프로 나오니 보기에 편리함

Thank you to developer for creating this app! It must really hard for you to gain money. But I will donate sometimes in the future. I promise.

Just one more thing, can you create a feature so that I can add photos in the journal? It will be really helpful to me, because I can create memories.

😊😊😊

title: Best Tracker Ever
body:
I think this might be my first ever review on an app but this is too good to be quiet. I’m a Premium user, have been for the past 5-ish years. It’s so simple and uncluttered. I can compare the trend of my habits over days, months, years.

I can see my streaks with habits. There’s this tiny feature where if you tap on the current day/yesterday, you can track habits in rapid succession without having to tap the row below. It may be a small thing but it really makes the user experience loads better.

You can categorise habits, add notes to each track, and set reminders (I haven’t used this last feature a lot though)

But yeah, if you’re thinking of a habit tracker, just pay for this. It’s worth it!

title: poor month view
body:
I tested 7 of these habit/ritual tracker apps.  this was 2nd worse and 2nd most expensive mmm....

this app was most complicated to use of all

key points
1 no ability to tap to switch from week ti calender view.  I prefer calender as gives bigger context than week.  their month is a row, plain silly to use as too tiny to tap

2 no current streak, longest streak and total in quick listing of all habits 

3 no ability to tap planned days, say 26 days in 30 -- I can do my activity on any day just need to be 26 within 30.  I like to plan these days, then tap when done

4 takes two taps rather than 1 tsp to say I'm done.  cumbersome
they have tried to make the tracker better by asking you to specify skip or not done.  way way too much maintenance.  felt like an accountant.  rather simpler, for me, to put your Programme in, then 1 tap to say done that day.

5 no ability to specify by visual que the activity you did (eg easy run, hill run, long run) (by change in colour shade for day - very light blue, light blue, mid blue

6 no nice ritual layout view (by rows) as in ritual app

title: Absolutely love it!
body:
Great little app which acts a bit like a diary of your progress - on whatever field you choose. Instead of reminding you to do the things you should do, it let you „close the day” whith a summary of things completed (or not). In the long run - if used honestly and everyday - it gives you interesting insights into the REAL stats about your life and activities. 
Positive streaks keeps you motivated, long gaps of things not done gently makes you come back to the routine. 
If you dont like to be „pushed” by constant notifications of what must be done, but rather like to keep self discipline by looking into the recorded past track of events - this app will be perfect!

title: Автоматические резервные копии за 1к рублей? Обойдётесь
body:
Купил это приложение, чтобы не париться и не бояться потерять данные. И что вы думаете? 

Переустановил систему на Маке. Заново устанавливаю все приложения. Захожу с полной уверенностью, что все мои данные сохранились и понимаю, что ничего подобного. Резервные копии надо было создавать вручную. Класс. 

Но единица — не только за это. Приложение просто не стоит своих денег. Интерфейс не очень удобны. Уступает бесплатным сервисам. 

Да и в целом ощущения от использование скорей отрицательное. Очень не рекомендую использовать. Берите что-нибудь бесплатное.

title: Предложение по улучшению
body:
Уважаемый разработчик, спасибо за вообще приложение. Оно очень сильно помогает мне укреплять свою дисциплину и двигаться к своим целям. Хотел бы рассказать о проблеме, с которой я столкнулся и тем, как я её решаю сейчас.

Мне по душе работать с блоками привычек, когда одна привычка тянет за собой выполнение второй, а та в свою очередь — выполнение третей. Выполнение одной — триггер для старта другой. И чтобы сделать такие блоки у себя я создал отдельные привычки, которые я не заполняю. Я прописал там время для ориентира, но и это не так важно для меня как смысловое разграничение этих блоков. 

Пожалуйста, рассмотрите мой случай как один из потенциальных user flow использования вашего приложения

title: Очень полезная программа!
body:
Раньше печатал себе чеклисты и отмечал их вручную на стене. 
Теперь где бы я ни был, можно следить за своими результатами в любое время.
Что не хватает, так это количественных показателей.
Можно отмечать только да и нет (зеленый/красный), а хотелось бы увидеть градиенты. 
Например сон: 5 часов - красный, 8 - зеленый. А все, что в промежутке - градиентом от красного к зеленому. 
Или алкоголь: 0 мл - зеленый, 200 мл - красный. В промежутке градиент. И т.д.

И спасибо за программу.

title: Небольшие пожелания по развитию
body:
Я искал такое приложение уже давно, и оценив аналоги, выбрал Way Of Life.
Сразу же купил себе премиум. Приложение близко к идеальному, и явно лучше конкурентов, но есть вещи которые я хотел бы видеть:
1) Синхронизация через iCloud. В идеале, необходима синхронизация через несколько облачных сервисов. Мне лично удобнее через iCloud, у меня нет дропбокса. 
2) Версия для Mac, либо веб-версия. Предпочтительнее конечно версия для Mac)
Плюс настольная версия позволит вам реализовать более мощный анализ журналов, графики будут больше, нагляднее как минимум)

body:
Программа шикарная. Скачала и через 30 секунд после открытия купила полную версию! Она того стоит! У меня больше 100 заданий на день. Очень мотивирует и помогает контролировать себя с легкостью. Раньше записывала все тоже самое в тетрадь, что не очень удобно. Спасибо большое за приложение! Оно облегчило мне жизнь и уверена, что она поможет мне стать намного лучше!)

Кроме того, у меня есть несколько идей по поводу улучшения программы. Прочтите, может быть Вам понравится и вы вынесете изменения в программу 
1. Было бы неплохо если бы можно было бы сделать заданий на 1 раз в неделю, а не на каждый день. (Например: поменять постельное белье) и 1 раз в месяц (сделать генеральную уборку)
2. Еще было бы намного удобнее, если бы можно было нажимать на задание и там появлялись подпункты. 
Например:
Есть фрукты
 -скушать банан
 -скушать яблоко
 И т.д.  Чтобы отдельно можно было бы контролировать каждый подпункт, при этом удобнее в пользовании было. 
3. В списке идей можно было бы удалять то, что уже выбрал. Чтобы несколько раз одно задание не было в списке на день

Вот. Это вроде все

Спасибо большущее любимое приложение теперь!!!!!

2) сделать "плотность", например у меня по плану четыре рабочие сессии, а я уговорил себя только на две. 
3) добавить возможность назначать время под цель и/или отдельную страничку, где я могу накидать свой план по выполнения на завтра. 
4) в заметках сделать логическое упорядочивание мыслей, например как древо в структуре папок windows, только минималистично( отличный пример программа workflowy). 
5) добавить в сводку сколько я прибавил/убавил в процентах за такую-то дистанцию по сравнению с аналогичной дистанцией в прошлом как суммарно, так и выборочно по цели.

title: Годная работа! Good job!
body:
Это приложение - одно из тех немногих, к которым вы будете возвращаться каждый день, порой с хорошими новостями (о, да я сегодня уже как 7 дней не питаюсь фастфудом!), а порой не очень хорошими (опять я сожрал тонну бабушкиных пирожков - надо остановиться). А потом посмотрите на все в графическом виде и поймете, что либо вы славно поработали над собой, либо... не очень славно! Главное тут - честность: себе врать не вариант!
Большая благодарность разработчикам!
~~~~~~~~~~~~
This application is the one from a short list of apps to which you will return every day, sometimes with good news (oh, today is a week since I've stopped eating fast food), and sometimes with not very good (again I ate a tonne of granny's pies - I should stop). And then you look at everything in graphical view and understand, that you've done a glorious work to improve oneself or you've done... not very glorious. The main thing is to be honest: lying to oneself isn't a right thing!
Many thanks to the developers!

title: Great app!
body: I like the app a lot! It’s easy to use and understand. I would like to be able to track more habits on the free version, but I understand why it’s limited. I use this every day and I actually think three habits is enough.  If you want to track more habits and are ambitious enough to follow through with updating and changing them I think it’s worth it to spend some money on it. (Especially now, since it’s cheaper because of the coronavirus) I really like that you can take notes on each day and the fact that notes you took earlier will be saved and you can click on them to use the Sam notes later. However, I wish there was a way to see everything written underneath too, because if I start with the same words I can’t tell the difference. A preview on the full sentences would be nice! I’ve seen that some users had trouble getting into the app, but I personally haven’t had any issues and I think it’s worth to try downloading the app to see if it works for you too, because I think it can be very helpful if you update and stick to the routines you decide to keep.

title: nice and simple
body:
I've used a few habit tracking apps including Coach.me (Lift) and Productive. But Way of Life is my favorite so far due to its simplicity and clean interface. I like how you can quickly see the overview of your all habits and quickly mark them off as done, not done, or skip. 

The app keep track of your streaks to reinforce sticking to your habits. You can add notes to your habits for the day, and see stats for your performance (haven't used this feature much yet, but it does looks pretty good).

Overall, the app is fast, simple, and it does what it's supposed to do: help track your habits quickly and effectively.

title: Please make this sync across devices!
body: I have used this app for years.  I don’t even know how many.  I feel like at least 10 years.  Every so often I reevaluate my listed habits — update etc.  That is when I think it would be awesome to have it on my phone and IPad.  I have tried everything to sync across devices.  But, it never works.  I then check out every single habit app there is.  I have purchased countless habit apps.  Nothing is ever as good.  I always come back. This is a great app.  A lot of helpful features but not so many it is overwhelming to learn.  There really is nothing that compares and I have looked and tried every habit app that syncs.  The simplicity is what makes it head and shoulders above the rest.  It is a brilliant design. I feel like years ago I read you were working on syncing across devices.  But it never happened.  It would be just that much better if I could use on my iPad and phone.  Please please please make it so it is easy to use on multiple devices!  Using it really has become my way of life.  Regardless, thanks for a great app.  I cannot think of any other app I have used as much or as long as this one.  So, I was going to give 4 stars but I will give 5 just for how long I have used it.  MAKE SYNC ACROSS DEVICES AVAILABLE- at this point I would pay to sync.

title: Good app, easy to use… few details could make it dynamite
body:
Just a few details could make even another step easier to use. 1-call the list of goals something besides a journal. “Journal” as a title if a group of goals isn’t proper use of the word journal. 2-repeat tapping on a goal should cycle the response if checkmark, x , skip, and blank, rather than having to move your finger to click on the icon (both should work). 3-when tapping on the icon response, default next action be the next goal, same date, if the date being recorded is today. If I am recording yesterday’s performance and click on X or checkmark, or Skip, the default should advance the mark (cursor to today… staying on the same goal.
4-if a NOTE has been created for a goal and a date, there should be some sort of badge or marker or shaded or outlined; as is, it is hard to see which goals and on which days there is a note.
These tweeks would make this App another big step better. I think the programmer has moved on and hasn’t modified or updated this App for quite awhile… but still is good!
author: Myron Mur

title: Great App for chaining progress
body:
I use a traditional to-do list that has a million features for projects and multi-step tasks.

But what that complex app is not great for is quick daily habits; that’s where Way of Life shines.

It’s great for chaining tasks (make the bed, take vitamin, etc) and a strong visual if you are completing or breaking those chained tasks. 

I also like the summary feature that can show how much of your dailies you completed per day, week, month. 

I did drop it a start because I wish it had a once a week option for tasks instead of having to skip 6 days just to mark one yes/no. Weekly things like “take trash to curb”. But I understand that might be a lot of programming for a feature not everyone would use. If they add “weekly” tasks it would be a 5/5 star review.

title: Best I’ve found !
body:
I’m glad I found this app after trying out many goal and habit apps. Most recently I was trying success wizard. And I mean I really gave it a good effort. It had nice tools for helping you gain clarity in your goals, but the day to day usability was not there for me. Plus too many bugs and didn’t seem to be developing. 

I’ve upgraded to an annual premium sub with way of life after just a day of the trial. Really like the ease of use and powerful simplicity! Already getting productive on my habits and successfully moving towards my goals. 

I’m also really encouraged by these reviews and seeing the dev team responding and taking feedback. Thanks !!

Wishlist: I’ll second what another user shared - the ability to set # of days for journals would be a massively helpful upgrade. Currently, every habit/journal is essentially “daily” with ability to skip manually. Not bad, but makes the trends a bit funky - example: 3 journals = 21 days … if you have 3 different exercise journals, 3 days strength training, 2 days cardio, and 2 days yoga that’s really only 7 days. Would be cool if the trend could reflect that, especially when you start adding more than just 3 journals. 

Thanks for a good experience so far !! 📈

In theory, I could tag habits by day of the week or time block for a custom list which would make tracking a lot easier and more rewarding in terms of actually achieving behavior change, but there is a bug in the display of habits/journals that makes this difficult… when I filter by a tag, it sorts by order of creation, not by the custom sort order… so my habit list which goes in order by time block is jumbled up within my time block and really confusing to look at and kind of derails me. The ability to filter by tag is a key driver for me to upgrade from Habitshare (free) is a key driver to get me to shell out for a yearly $30 subscription. 

I tried reaching out to their support desk during the free trial but nobody answered. It looks like someone is answering reviews of the app, so maybe someone will see this and fix the bug, because this app would really help me and I’d like to be able to use it.

title: Helps me improve habits & make good decisions!
body:
I’ve been using this app on and off for years now but have been using it very consistently for a couple years straight now and it has had a tremendous positive impact on my life. Having a really quick and easy way to log my patterns and behaviors each day allows me to be more aware and accountable to myself. Visible seeing exactly how many days in a month I log a “bad” habit makes me more inspired to improve it, and seeing the number count up on my streaks makes me want to keep them going through healthy competition with myself, because I don’t want to break my streak! It helps motivate to be able to see you milestones broken down into specific numbers and statistics. Clean design, quick and easy to use, and I love the variety of ways you can display the data.

This app has enabled me so much in my own personal growth and health, and I recommend it regularly and now have a bunch of friends using it and seeing improvement in their own lives as well.

I cannot recommend it highly enough! Thanks for all you do, Lars!

title: Invaluable
body: I have used to app for some six or seven years, and find it tremendously helpful. I am sure my life would be less without it (in fact I did think I had outgrown it at one point and was proven quite wrong). I tell people about it all the time. It's a great way, for one, to not get hung up on all-or-nothing thinking (with perfect streaks and so on), and to see that even when you feel like you are failing to some degree, you may still be improving from what came before. And of course, it is perfect just for the simple business of doing the day-to-day tracking itself, just for the accountability and record keeping. In the rare instance I have needed to contact the developer, it might have taken a while for them to initially get back (I think they are just one person, so be patient) but when they did I found them to be tremendously helpful and open to feedback. An absolutely solid app.

My one critic is that the app could’ve had more interaction. Even something like confetti after a week of maintaining a good habit or making progress. title: Filler free, but…
body: I've got a bad habit of looking for a habit tracker, but this about hits the sweet spot. Fat-free, simple …but still gives the data nerd in me some info to peruse once populated. And the one-time buy is a huge, huge plus for me. The navigation can be a little wiggly getting used to it, as is flipping the script on "yes" v "no", but nothing crushing. There are one or two aspects of the navigation that appear to do nothing (or I'm not as bright as I thought) or are vestigial, and support has yet to reply, but I don't seem to be missing anything in making it work and track for right now. Other than that, nice and clean and self-contained. In and out without a lot of pointless distractions that build bad habits while working on others. Looking forward to filling it up to keep getting that bigger picture and for where this might go and what else they might do. If you want a tracker without overkill data and cutesy eye-candy fluff, this might be for you.

title: Very nice, but lacking some much desired features
body:
I really like the simplicity of this app, and especially love and respect that the developer did not fall into the subscription model; buy-once and forget is so great for the user.

I will say that it is missing a few key features that would really complete it for me.

Would it be possible to add in an option make some journal items occur less frequently than every day of the week? For instance, there are some things that I want to target doing once a week, or twice a week. To be able to track those as well as my daily habits, all from a single app, would be amazing. Currently I have to mix-and-match with other apps to really review a week of my life the way I'd like to.

Devs; is this possible? It would get a 5-star review from me. If N-times a week is too complicated to include, simply having the option of a once-a-week journal entry would be awesome. 

What I'm currently doing is making journal entries that say something like "exercised, or took intentional rest day". This technically turns it into an every-day item, but it's kind of a non-ideal workaround to the preferred "exercised this week" option that could exist. 

Chains could work the exact same way, with respect to consecutive weeks rather than consecutive days

Thanks for reading, abs for the hard work!

title: Old faithful / Gold Standard
body:
I’ve possibly tried every habit app, and keep coming back to this one. I find it causes me more anxiety to deal with all the bells and whistles of the other apps than just straightforward check boxes - I did it / I didn’t / I’m skipping. For others I felt like I needed a habit app just to do all it took to record my habits! 
However what makes this a gold standard is that in addition to the simple and intuitive interface, it has one of the best data outputs of any of the apps I’ve tried. Actually I think it is the best. 
I also like that whenever there’s an update, it feels like the app developers are writing you a personal note to let you know what they did and why they did it :)
I know these types of apps can’t be one size fits all, but I wish more people would try this because everyone I’ve recommended it to really loves it! Ps -The only bells and whistle type of thing I kind of missed was having cute icons, but then I realized I can just add emojis at the beginning of each task which is actually way better because then I can make it much more specific compared with some the weird icon packs from other apps! PPS - the recent different theme update sealed the deal because it now looks just as cool as all the ones with too much fluff! Great work developers 👏🏻 👏🏻

title: Using it for years
body:
I’ve used Way of Life for years now. It does its job diligently, and I’ve appreciated the improvements over the years.

However, the lack of syncing has become problematic for me. I know on the surface, syncing for a habit tracker may seem like overkill which can be easily skipped.

But I keep a separate, old device beside my bed for catching notes and ideas … and Way of Life is only on my main phone.

So when I’m dozing off to sleep and remember something I need to add to a tracker, I have to make a separate note somewhere else (usually in Things), then in the morning be mindful enough to put the note in its proper place in WoL. 

I do this regularly enough that it has become annoying, especially when I have multiple notes to add to different trackers. WoL is the type of app where you want to track a note when it happens, not create a sprawling system to keep it in order.

I’ve tried other trackers, several of which have sync, but prefer WoL’s simplicity. I just need this simplicity to sync across multiple devices.

title: Almost perfect
body:
I have been using this app for ~2 years. It really helped me reflect on my life and encouraged me to keep up with my right habits. The UI is keep getting better and easier to use. Love the option that it automatically jump to the next open entry. Here are a few features I would love to see. 
1. A way to set goals like 3 times a week or once every month - very useful for tracking exercises or anything that you don’t necessarily want or need to do everyday 
2. Ability to make notes or entry for future days - eg. I travel for work a lot and like to track which day I’m away from home. So if I know I will be gone for 5 days, it would be easier to enter they all at once. 
3. For the same example, it would be great if I could set a not exceeded goal. So I could track no more than 15 days a month away from home
4. Integration with Apple Health and other health apps. So I don’t need to duplicate the entry of tracking how many days I workout. 
I’m sure any app have rooms to improve. But overall I love this app. Great job for the developers behind this app. Big thanks to you all. It has helped change my lifestyle and help me be a better me!

title: Helpful! Encouraging!
body:
I find this app the best for habit forming. I bought several to test out which one I would like the best since forming a good habit is so critical to healthy living. This app has a notification on the app (red bubble with number of habits waiting to be completed that day). The notification is helpful to remind you as the day goes on and you can see the number go down. 
I made the mistake of having 7 habits and it grew to 10. I'm down to 3 now since I was feeling defeated when I didn't accomplish all 10. Simple habits like "make your bed in the a.m." or "take vitamins" or "exercise for 10 minutes". I was sick for a few days but I checked off that I exercised and took my vitamins and wrote a note in that box that I would have exercised and taken vitamins if I wasn't puking. Or you can hit the skip button and write a note why you had to skip. If you didn't have to skip, check the "X" and use that as an oppty to get better. It's not a negative mark on you, it's an oppty to get more green check marks and improve. Keep it simple and support and encourage yourself.

title: Better than ever!!!
body:
Been using this app for about 3 years, and it’s now been about 2 years since I last left a review.  Through steady updates, this continues to be the best habit/task tracking app out there for me.   It’s simplicity, function, and charm just can’t be matched.  

The most recent update involves some nifty design changes so I thought I’d update my 2 year old review.  I really do love the newer update!  It brings so many design elements that make the app much more beautiful and modern. Buttons, journals, and charts look so much cleaner and more modern.  I also love the new themes!  The dark themes are more favs, but the other ones really do bring out different moods and vibes from app.  

With each update, the developer brings something new to the table, which just goes to show how hard working and dedicated the devs are — not only to the app, but to its users.  This continues to be a quality app that I’ve used everyday for 3 years and I consider to be an essential for all iOS users.  I hope the dev continues to bring us quality and keep up the good work!  Every bit of praise and success this app gets is well deserved.

title: Just what I wanted
body:
I wanted a simple “yes I did it” sort of tracker. But one that I could mark off the next day and not necessarily at the time I was doing it. This has reminders if you want them, but I like that I can set one reminder to update the whole list instead of being bugged about every item. I want the motivational nudge of a streak without the irritation of reminders or stress of losing “credit” because I was living my life and not updating my app one day. 

Love that you can mark as done, not done, or skipped... as in didn’t do on purpose. And the tracking of not doing negative things is a first in the recommendations. I tried a dozen habit minders and this was the only suggesting that and asking if it’s a positive or negative item (for example, tracking not smoking or not binge eating). 

Happily paid for the full version with unlimited items.

title: It works, life change happens.
body:
One of the only apps I started using, saw value from immediately, and have kept using for years now. It’s a clever way to make and track any type of goal. Life change is possible, and Way of Life is a strong companion to that. The combo of simplicity in UI, visualization of progress, and ability to add context through journals and descriptions makes it just right for me. 

Some habits I’ve broken and made with WoL as a companion:
- have a morning routing
- making my bed every day on waking
- journaling daily
- sobriety
- meditation
- daily mini exercise before showering
- gratitude

Update Oct 2018
I’ve been using WOL for over 4 years now. It’s still as powerful today for me as it was when I started. When I’m using it, I’m healthier. When I’m not, I’m declining. The life pattern is obvious, and actually WOL make it visually obvious. Thanks WOL, you’re a life changer.

title: Excellent Choice
body:
(I have no idea why Apple would have removed my earlier — positive — review. Fortunately, I keep copies of them.)

Way of Life is an apt name for an app that is designed to help you change your habits. Like most apps in its category, Way of Life encourages you to build chains (from Jerry Seinfeld) by completing good habits; unlike most, however, you can also pursue the destruction of bad habits.

That feature helps the app stand out, but another feature that I like is the ability to skip habits without breaking the chain. There are some habits that concern me only when I'm at home, so when I travel I don't want to lose my streak.

Multiple, custom reminders is a feature that I have to have. It's in there. I can't understand why more apps bent on ensuring you get things done don't implement them. And notes allow you to document the good and bad in each day's struggle.

I love the way that Way Of Life presents your data. You can see a week or a month at a time when updating your data, and you can filter the list by only those left remaining for the day or by specific sets of habits (using tags). And with an eye on building chains, the app shows your current progress and best effort for each habit right on the main screen.

Where the app disappoints, however, is its inability to set a habit frequency different from once a day. Blog three times a week? Drink eight cups of water a day? Way of Life can't help you track a habit like that and workarounds don't satisfy.

With its ease-of-use, though, Way of Life is a a excellent choice for building habits in your life.

Update: the new Today widget is largely useless, since I cannot check off habits from there.

title: Initially Excited But...
body:
I should've played around with the free version for longer than 10 seconds before I hastily paid full price. 

I was in initially excited about the app because of the visual data, I need that kind of motivation. However, my excitement level diminished when I learned there aren't a whole lot of choices for the custom journals. For example, I want track drinking 8 glasses of water a day; right now the only way to set it up is by the week, I want to track 8 glasses of water daily, as I would taking medications or vitamins. For $5, I should have the option to track something at whatever interval (daily, weekly, or monthly) and goal (3 days/week, 8/day, daily)
and not have to adhere to the week format with the default of tracking 3/week. I think it's silly that this was not already an option, at least for the paid version.

I saw in another review that that person uses an app called Productivity for daily habit tracking, but I'm trying to consolidate apps and not have 5 different ones for the same thing. I would prefer, since I have already paid for this one, to be able to have a little more flexibility when creating journals. If this app could do that, I would have given it 5 stars.

title: Love this app!
body:
This app is exactly what I was looking for! I wanted to be able to track the interaction of certain external factors and my responses with good and bad habits. For example, did I eat more junk food on the days that I had gotten too little sleep? Or, did I sleep poorly in the days preceding my menstrual period,  or after a bad day at work. This app allows me to see at a glance how these factors are correlating or not correlating over the course of a week or a month. I also love that you can make notes relevant to any particular habit on any particular day, to review what's working and what's not working in adhering to your habits.
An individual habit can be classified as a good habit or a bad habit, which I also like. 
I find the app is super-simple to use. I can mark my habits for the day in about 3 seconds, if I don't leave any notes.

Here's my set-up: For developing good habits as part of daily routines, I use a different app called Productive. For reasons I won't go into here, that app excels in that role. But developing good habits is a different experience from breaking bad ones, and when it comes to bad habits, that's where Way of Life shines. It's clean, elegant, and reliable, and the red-and-green indicators make it crystal clear when you've slipped up and when you did well. The various ways of viewing the data are enormously motivating and a real help. I am every bit as pleased with Way of Life as a tracker of bad habits as I am with Productive as a tracker of the good. They're a great team.

title: Effective but needs usability and export tweaks

I've been using Way of Life daily for over two years. It's still surprisingly effective as a gentle evening reminder to check in with my habits and goals. 

The interactions for rapidly inputting several answers, even for one day with multiple goals or catching up for a day or two ago, aren't as fluid or intuitive. It consciously feels like too many taps.

I'm a bit disappointed in the lack of an iPad app and missing iCloud sync. I didn't realize my data was only stored locally (so if my phone is lost or wiped, the data is gone). The paid upgrade for more tracking and data export was a no-brainer. I do wish the export was automatic. I rarely remember to export to Dropbox myself and I'd hate to lose all this data. 

Still love and happily support the app!

title: Really helps w/Triggers by Goldsmith
body:
I have read a number of habits books, and I've bought a fair number of apps--most of which now sit in the cloud and do nothing for me. Why? Because they were a pain in the a** to set up and were too interlocked with complicated goal systems that never helped motivate me to achieve what I wanted to.  Enter: Way of Life. This elegant, deceptively simple app, however, seems to work beautifully because it is so easy to get up and running that I've actually used it a lot. It's easy to track things, and it gives you a nice "ding" as a reward for doing something three days in a row. Cheesy as this may sound, I now love the ding and am rewarding myself with my own Pavlovian pellet--self-esteem--every time I hear it.

If you have tried a bunch of things that haven't made a dent or changed you, read Marshall Goldsmith's Triggers and use this app to track the daily questions you're supposed to use.

My only nit/quibble with the app is that I wish the text fields where you enter the item you'd like to track ran longer. Using Goldsmith's system, I track behaviors using questions focused on effort rather than accomplishment: "Did I do my best to write today?" (Goldsmith wants you to use a spreadsheet and record a number, which I will never be caught dead doing.) This is way simpler and, therefore, way easier to use. Ergo, more likely to be used.  

For already converted Goldsmith fans: I use the acronym "DIDMB" for "Did I do my best?" and very short phrases of text. To make it simpler, I even put emojis at the beginning of the labels to make them easier to scan. (Don't laugh!) Goldsmith's system actually works, and this clean, simple app really helps.

title: Best in Class App
body:
Way of Life is a simple, flexible tool for tracking desired or unwanted daily behaviors.

Typically when I get an app I immediately find a limitation or unnecessary complexity.  That happened for me with all other daily behavior tracking apps on the app store but not with this one.  

You declare the specific behaviors and whether they're good or bad.  Then, daily, you mark whether you did it, didn't do it or if it did not apply.  It's straightforward to use and easy to review.  

As someone whose bad habits sneak up on him and who tends not to recognize my good ones, this tool has been very valuable.  I could not recommend it more.

I often use skips rather than misses so that I can see how many days I've done a habit rather than how many days in a chain I've maintained. Graphs are detailed and customizable. I use it throughout the day, and everyday to monitor progress that I'm making for all aspects of my life including: Exercise, Education, Finances, Christian Faith, Client Actions Taken. I have between 50-100 topics I track every day. I use both the weekly and monthly view to see my progress. I commonly will add brief notes. The note section overview is very helpful to review comments you've made on previous days, weeks and months. The stats screen is a great tool to monitor your progress for an individual category as well as for your global progress. This system will clearly illuminate your strengths, weaknesses, wins, and areas that need your focus.  During the final week of each month I review everything to modify or delete the topics I am currently tracking in preparation for the next month. I've found it is helpful to group the topics tracked by category.

title: Missing 2 Key Feature
body:
Nov 2016 update, I purchased Way of Life after my other app (Good Habits) lost my data. 

I purchased WoL because of the backup to Dropbox feature - which works well.  Nevertheless after only one month I'm already looking at other apps.  WoL still has a few major issues.  First, you still gets advertisements after paying 3.99.  Second, you can't edit a habit name from a negative to positive and vice versa.  You have to delete and start over.

— Original update —

I was really impressed with the Ui, simplicity, number of features, charts and exporting capabilities. My guess is that 95% of the users would rate this 5 stars.  However, for me, it's missing two key features.  1. There isn't a way to reorder habits (daily tasks). 2.  You can only go back one day.  So if you forgot to create an entry 2 days ago, you are out of luck.  If these two features are added, I'll change my review to 5 stars and gladly pay the $4.99.

title: Thank you for helping me build good habits!
body:
I used the free three habit tracking for flossing, midday prayer, and exercising. 

Simple. Clear. Elegant. And therefore emotionally satisfying no matter my energy level or busy-ness level for that day. 

A few weeks ago I purchased the full app and added in some food goals. I tend to over commit in making To Do lists and daily plans, so I told myself I wouldn't add anything else, but it is so pleasing to see those streaks of green that within a week I had 22 items in about five tag categories. Here's some examples - Exercise: mini-aerobic. Aerobic every two days. Abs & Stretch. - Food: Broccoli or Spinach 2X per week. - Flossing am. Flossing pm - Inflows: Text Count Zero. Voicemail Zero. eMail <20. THANK YOU

ps Glad to read the great update suggestions from other happy Way Of Life users....

Four months later:
The book Changology points out something true for me: changing the objectives keeps me interested, motivated, and propelled towards the goal. 

So, I'm on the second revision of using this app since my last review. 

Now I use it for evening and exercise objectives - and for reflection, utilizing the comment feature. I also list what I'm grateful for in a comment each evening. 

I'm sure I will always use this app.

title: Superior to just tracking streaks
body:
Instead of just tracking consecutive streaks--which the app also does--Way of Life has trend graphs that help you visualize total improvement over time. 

So if I had a daily goal and I only ever racked up 3 consecutive days, I might feel lousy about how I was doing. But with Way of Life I could see that over the last 6 months those 3-day streaks had grown more and more frequent, and that I was actually improving my consistency a great deal. 

That's very, very helpful to me. It helps me stick with it when otherwise I might get discouraged. Which is the best thing, after all, isn't it?

title: Useful app but could use a few improvements
body:
Great app for tracking various things--habits, moods, food, exercise, health! I like how flexible you can be in creating things to track. You can look at your tracked items in a weekly or monthly view, which is useful. The different statistics and graphs of your progress are really useful, too. The fact that you can "skip" days is helpful for tracking weekly goals (which the app doesn't let you do otherwise) or giving yourself a break now and then. You can also add some notes to each daily tracked item, though this isn't really useful (yet) since there's no easy overview of notes or search function. There's a backup-to-Dropbox option for your trackers, but you can also choose to delete your trackers and start fresh. :)

Biggest current annoyance: there are no dates in the app, just days of the week. Would be really useful to know when things happened, beyond just "7 Mondays ago" or whatever. 

Other features I would like are weekly goals or the ability to group goals.

Overall, pretty neat app with room for further developments.

One note for improvement: It would be great to be able to track habits that are not daily-based. For example, if I want to meditate 3 times a week, I can either select Yes, No or Skip for the daily status of this habit. However, I feel like No is too harsh and Skip does not truly account for my needs. I'd like to see the trends of my actual success without looking like I'm missing most days or skipping most days.

I'd like to see partial week, weekly and monthly habit tracking (like taking the train to work 2 times/week or visiting a local park 3 times/month).

Otherwise, wonderful app!

title: Great at what it does.
body:
Still great.

Update 4/23/14: new
  This app is really good at helping you track things when you really want to try some new habits and see if they're helping you out or not.

   I started a new fitness, sleep and health routine and this app shows you just how often you really get it done. If I'm on track and I don't feel better, those habits aren't helping. If I'm on track and feeling better they are. The app really helps you track whether the changes you make to your daily habits are really helping or not. 

---------

For what it's designed to do, it does it simply and perfectly....really.

If you're committed to creating the good habits and avoiding the bad ones, it can really help you stay mindful of your simple daily goals.  

If you're not really that committed, it probably won't get you there, but it will help you keep trying.

body:

Requests/Suggestions: 
1) I love the new archive feature, but I still wish we could set deadlines/due dates for things that are time sensitive. After the due date, it would make sense if the item was automatically archived. 

2) When a drop down menu says "ALL" it should show EVERYTHING including the archived items. Right now it only shows active items. I think this could be fixed easily by just adding an ACTIVE drop down menu. Then ALL could truly display ALL. 

3) I appreciate that we can view archived notes, but I would really like to see charts for archived items as well. Honestly, It would be great to add an archive drop down option to all screens. (journals/trends/notes)

title: Great app with a few things missing
body: I love this app, it's fantastic and I wholeheartedly give it 5 stars. But I'm disappointed and that's my fault for not paying enough attention before I bought it, but the reason I purchased was I thought it had a certain feature and it does not. I love the fact that we can skip a day so it doesn't count towards the streak/goal. However, I have to manually figure out when I've hit my goal for the week. For example, I want to do strength training 3 times per week. As I'm marking along each day of the week, I need to count my green spots and determine when I've hit my goal. I'd like it if when entering my goal I can tell the app "I want to do this 3 times per week." Then the app automatically calculates me as 100% success after there are 3 greens in that week. Also, would be awesome if it showed in the reporting "current streak 5, total completions 35, longest streak 21" or something of that nature. And min/max would be great too. For example, I want to eat dessert no more than 2x per week, so count me bad starting at the 3rd, or on the other side of it, I want to do cardio at least 3x per week, so start me good at 3 but let me do up to 7 without showing me bad. Other than that, amazing app, thanks.

title: Perfect, Intuitive, Easy to Use, Love it!!!
body:
I use this app every single day. Whoever designed it is brilliant! - Thank you! 
The concept is shockingly simple and works perfectly: 
-Is it bad for you? - Is it good for you? Depending on the answer, you will mark it red or green, if you've done it today. If doing it or not doing it today wasn't part of your goal, then you can skip it by marking it blue, and it won't be taken into account for calculated trends!
Isn't that brilliantly simple?! Minimum time to set up. Minimum time to mark your "deeds" everyday.
Love it. This app has virtually no flaws.

title: Best time management app
body:
I have downloaded well over 100 productivity apps. Many of those apps were very unproductive, and difficult to use.
This app is very user-friendly. I especially liked the simple green-and-red system, that way there are no excuse for when you just won't follow up and are not improving your lifestyle.
The graphs and charts help show you how much much progress you've had over the course of a week, a month, or even a year. This is very motivating when you are trying to create a new habit.
I'm very confident that after 60 days there will be no need to keep track of your new found habits. 
Lastly, I will say this to you.
All apps and programs are effective as long as you are consistent. So I will suggest you turn on the notifications setting because this way you will know what is keeping from being successful. It is ultimately up to you to keep up with your tasks and to create and maintain good healthy habits.

Have a way to automatically skip days. For example, I only go to spinning on Saturdays. I don't like to go in each day and mark it as skipped. 

Have a way to so combo graphs so I can see the days I went to the gym and the days I went running on the same graph. 

developers- I'd pay 1.99 at most for this app the way it stands. 2.99 if my wish list items were added.

title: It's okay…
body:
It is limited to 3 items, and then you have to update if you want to add more.   Five dollars is a bit too much to pay for a full version of this app, in my opinion. I mean, "Asphalt7 - Heat" is the most detailed, action-packed app in the store, and IT is only $0.99. 

I didn't see where we could add explanations of habits. I DID see that we could add explanation of skipped days. 

It could use sub folders. For instance, click on "exercising", which drops down to reveal "weights", "Jumping Jacks", "sit-ups", etc.   Or "Self Mutilation" drops down to reveal "smoking", "drinking", "playing with cat", etc. This is then figured out in percentages. For instance, if only "smoking" is checked in the "Self mutilation" folder, then 1/3 is green and 2/3 is red. (Friends don't let friends tease the cat drunk).  Not everything in life is black and white (errr...red and green).  Maybe this can be optional.

It could use sound effects. Like cheering when you select green and booing and hissing when you choose red.   When you open the chart, you get either musical revelry with crowds cheering or doomsday music (dum-da-da-dummm) with crowds booing, depending on the good/bad ratio.  Maybe accompanied with a brief "Good job! You're doing it!" Or "Try again! You can do this!" screen splashes. This will encourage us to do better (or cheat). 

Just a few ideas; getting it a bit closer to becoming a $5.00 app (really, dudes, you should drop the price to $2.99 at the most).

The "free for three items or less" deal is sneaky, as that is the limit after which adding more items degrades the ease of using the app notably, as the screen no longer fits all items and buttons and folding/unfolding per-day buttons makes everything jump around rather chaotically.

It's hard to design a really easy-to-use app. This is not a great success. It lets you do the job, but it not joyfully.

title: Best habit app.

Nice fast interface is better than other apps with complex interfaces. But it could be cleaned up a bit further.  The journal input bar pops up between habits. Put it at the bottom and highlight the selected habit (and day) or grey out the others. Then it would be easier to scroll and pick habits.  Once the habit is selected and the input bar is showing, we don't need to see the journal-trend-notes menu bar. Make it one or the other and it would give you space to make the journal input bar big enough to include all of the journal editing buttons at once (like "done" and "erase"). That's my wishlist.  Thanks for listening!

I used the free version for a month and then tried a bunch of other apps and chose to pay for this one. I agree that it could be a little cheaper, but it was totally worth it to me.

title: Changed my life!
body:
I used other habit apps before but none changed anything of me, except this one!

I am self-employed and worked as a freelance writer, procastination can be a problem for me, sometimes I spent the whole day doing nothing, my editor would email me on the deadline and asked me for an article. I felt so sorry but I simply couldn't get enough motivation to do it. 

Then I read a book called Now Habit, and decided to change my procastination, by using an app, or a better one. 

Based on the many good reviews of this app, I decided to give it a go.

Two hours after I downloaded this app, I paid for the full version. I like the interface and design, and most important, I want to see if paying the app would actually motivate me more to get things done.

I broke down my tasks in smaller unit (e.g. instead of writing "exercise", I added "push-ups", "stretching", "abs workout", "reading for at least 30 mins", etc. Now I have 23 items on my list, it may sound a bit long, it's more like a routine for me, but some take only 5 seconds to finish (e.g. "wake up right after hearing the alarm clock"), some may take a bit longer (e.g. "write a short article", "learn Tibetan")...

I finished all the tasks almost everyday in the past 38 days, and now I feel these became are my habits, it would probably difficult to stop doing any of them. 

I would highly recommend you to buy it, and also consider the paid version as well, the developer deserves to be paid for his great effort. 

PS: it would be nice if the list can be synced to iCloud, or every access from desktop browser.
